chapter: Early career: vaudeville and Kansas City
title: Reno Club hours and cabaret format
summary: Basie says the long 8 p.m. to 5 a.m. shift happened only on special nights, and that the Reno Club was a cabaret.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: All right. And -- okay, so -- is it true that you played 24 hours a day? No, how --
-- that you played from 8 p.m. to 5 a.m. or something like that?
No. No, it's only one night, time, we did that, just when we played with a special show or something. That's just when we'd work a 12-hour (inaudible).
Just one night that happened? So that that wasn't the run of the thing, then, that you were playing?
Because you couldn't have done it. I mean, could you?
Hardly, huh? I see. All right, did shows begin at the Reno? Would you begin a show? I mean, was it --
At the Reno Club. I don't know anything -- I mean, I've never been to Kansas City. I don't really know much about it.
It was a cabaret, oh. And so --
-- came back to this Reno Club? Cabaret? Nightclub performers? Singers? Dancers? The same as it would be in New York?
